title: Jalisco Governor Unleashes Repression – Soberanía 128
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 128 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
open with their take on the repression in Jalisco, where Governor Pablo Lemus
and Movimiento Ciudadano are under fire after state police brutally cracked
down on a peaceful, family-friendly protest demanding clean water in
Guadalajara. The hosts detail the detentions — including a Rappi delivery
worker snatched off his motorcycle — the squalid conditions at Casa Jalisco,
and the political fallout, from Morena's push for impeachment to federal human
rights investigations. They trace Movimiento Ciudadano's lineage back to the
PRI and explain why the "party of the two lies" keeps revealing itself as the
"orange PAN."

Next, they discuss the IMSS workers' protests, with thousands marching in
Mexico City and 20+ cities demanding 7% of GDP for healthcare, better wages,
and medicines that actually reach the clinics. The hosts share their own
experience navigating the IMSS system and break down the long neoliberal
erosion of Mexican healthcare, and they call out the crocodile tears from the
same media outlets that spent decades cheering its privatization. The
conversation turns to a solution: tax the rich.

Then they cover the left and the internet. President Sheinbaum goes live on
Instagram and TikTok for the first time, calling for regulation of violent
online content and addressing Anabel Hernández's fake news about her marijuana
use. They also analyze Meta's electoral interference in Brazil's second round,
where Lula's campaign has denounced the blocking of his ads.

Losers and Haters takes aim at Francisco Garduño, former head of Mexico's
National Migration Institute, exonerated of charges in the Ciudad Juárez fire
that killed 40 migrants. An apology months late, a mural, and some training
modules — the hosts note that when there are no consequences, the conditions
that led to the tragedy continue.
